title: The naive framing: "is my config broken?"
text: Someone assumed a plug-in that won't show up means broken configuration. Usually, it's just stale read once when the session started. So, is my config broken or just out of date? Before

title: Three steps, in order
text: Deciding anything, Claude checks three things in order. What actually arrived in the plug-in mount, what flags Claude code was launched with, and what the startup log recorded. All three get collected before any explanation is offered. Then it walks a short list of

title: Five failure causes
text: Causes. The zip simply isn't there. It's there, but Claude code wasn't launched with a matching flag. Zip failed to extract. The plug-in's manifest file is malformed, often just a stray capital letter or space in the name, or the zip is fine, but the skill file's own header is broken. Two limits worth knowing.

title: Two limits
text: First, a session reads your configuration once when it starts. Flip a setting mid-chat and the fix is a new conversation, not a refresh of this one. Second, some of Claude code's startup errors go to a channel this diagnostic can't see. So, a clean-looking log doesn't guarantee nothing went wrong. title: Carry-out

title: Your turn
text: Sitting in /mnt/account_plugins, but the skill inside it isn't showing up. Walk me through what actually arrived, what you were launched with, and what the startup log says before telling me what's wrong. Then check three things. Does it collect all three before explaining anything? Does it say so if the log file is missing instead of skipping past it? And if you flipped the setting a few minutes ago, does it ask you to start a fresh conversation? Stale, not broken. Lay 'em in for bare.
